blindSummary: This country newly and explicitly criminalises: in March 2025 a provision of the founding charter imposed by the ruling military junta outlawed "LGBTQIA+ practices or any other unnatural behavior" for the first time. Junta rule, an insurgency invoking religious motives, and the absence of any recourse make the risk grave.
blindOutOfScope: The March 2025 criminalisation is brand new; enforcement remains undocumented.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): in March 2025 this country explicitly outlawed consensual same-sex acts for the first time - a provision of the junta's founding charter prohibits 'LGBTQIA+ practices or any other unnatural behavior' during a five-year transition. No specific penalties yet, but a 2023 draft penal code seeks up to 5 years for same-sex conduct, 20 years for conducting or witnessing a same-sex marriage ceremony, and 5 years for participating in or financing 'homosexual' organisations. Even before the charter, two women were prosecuted in 2023 under 'public indecency' provisions.

Foreign broadcaster live coverage (Dec 2022): lawmakers in this country backed a motion to criminalise same-sex relationships - brought by a single MP; it came weeks after a regional court acquitted two women of lesbianism charges because no legislation existed.
